clue.text: Dog caught soldier pinching gold

indicators.note: to pinch is to squeeze between finger and thumb, so the caught-plus-soldier letters hold the gold inside them

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
GI is an American soldier
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A thieving soldier is arrested for helping himself to gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinching' looks like theft, but it tells you to wrap the soldier round the gold; GI is US army slang for a private.
explanation.definitionFit: A corgi is a short-legged Welsh breed of dog, favoured by the late Queen.

clue.text: Open country reportedly producing this wine

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word for open land is heard, not seen

parts.note: a champaign is an expanse of open level countryside

explanation.surface: Open countryside is said to yield a wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' means CHAMPAIGN, a literary word for flat open country, said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is a sparkling white wine from the French region of that name.

clue.text: Of an exceptional quality that's by no means common

definitions.meaning: splendid, fit for a king
belonging to the monarch's family, not the common people

explanation.surface: Praise for something so fine it is not ordinary at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both regal in quality and of the monarchy rather than commoners.

clue.text: Such amenities for shoppers may be forthcoming

definitions.meaning: services provided inside a shop, like an in-house bakery
about to happen, as in 'surprises ...'

explanation.surface: Shop facilities that might be on the way.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both located inside a shop and coming up soon.

clue.text: Vessel built by leading people aware of latest trends

parts.note: leading lights are prominent people, so the plural noun alone stands for them
hip means fashionably in the know

explanation.surface: A ship constructed by trendy, prominent figures.
explanation.definitionFit: A lightship is a moored vessel carrying a beacon to warn shipping.

clue.text: Brought down to earth, like some of the gentry

definitions.meaning: brought an aircraft or a fish to the ground
the ... gentry own estates

explanation.surface: Gentlefolk brought back to reality.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both set down on the ground and owning land, as rural gentry do.

clue.text: Mean but understanding

definitions.meaning: avaricious, greedy
... an idea is understanding it

explanation.surface: Stingy yet perceptive.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both greedy for money and comprehending.

clue.text: Learner, after school, repeated English

indicators.note: after places the doubled letters behind the word for school

parts.note: to school someone is to train them

indicators.note: repeated means the abbreviation appears twice

explanation.surface: A pupil goes over English again after lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is a verb here, giving TRAIN, and 'repeated' doubles E.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee is someone learning a job.

clue.text: Unbelievers inflame so-called defender of the faith

parts.note: to heat is to make hot
Henry VIII was granted the title Defender of the Faith by the Pope

explanation.surface: Non-believers rouse the monarch who styles himself protector of the faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry VIII received the title Fidei Defensor, still on British coins as FD.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathenry is the collective body of pagans, or heathens taken together.

clue.text: Iron furniture

definitions.meaning: to iron clothes is to smooth them flat
a cupboard, especially for linen

explanation.surface: Metal furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to smooth out creases, and a large cupboard.

clue.text: Old country with deep chasm in one area

parts.note: an abyss is a bottomless pit
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A former land described as having a deep gorge somewhere within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Abyssinia is the former name of Ethiopia, hence an old country.

clue.text: Saw a daughter grow old

parts.note: to age is to grow old

explanation.surface: Someone watched their daughter getting older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' reads as the past tense of see, but it is the noun meaning a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, as is an adage.

clue.text: Restrain criticism, but check speed of own horses

definitions.meaning: to hold back from attacking someone as hard as one could
read literally: rein in one's Suffolk Punches, a breed of heavy draught horse

explanation.surface: Advice to go easy on criticism, and to rein in one's own horses.
explanation.walkthrough: A Suffolk Punch is a British breed of heavy cart horse, so to pull them is to hold them back.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to deliver criticism more gently than one could.

clue.text: Look for large waterbird

definitions.meaning: a ... is a look, as in 'take a ...'
the male goose is a large waterbird

explanation.surface: Searching for a big bird near water.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: an informal glance, and the male of the goose.

clue.text: Probationary period making a small number corrupt

parts.note: No is the short form of number
to vitiate is to spoil or corrupt

explanation.surface: A trial period that corrupts a few people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a small number' looks like a handful, but it is the abbreviation No.
explanation.definitionFit: A novitiate is the trial period served by a novice in a religious order.

clue.text: Worked in American hospital under constraint

definitions.meaning: an intern is a junior hospital doctor in the US, and served as one gives the verb
confined, as people held without trial in wartime

explanation.surface: Someone who worked in a US hospital was kept under restriction.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both served as a junior doctor and detained in confinement.

clue.text: Dog connected with scandal in racing area

parts.note: dirt is damaging gossip
to dog someone is to follow or track them

explanation.surface: A greyhound mixed up in scandal at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' looks like a greyhound, but it is the verb meaning to trail.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirt track is an unpaved course used for motorcycle or stock car racing.

clue.text: Creamy dessert out East, also known as main course

indicators.note: out means the compass letter is taken away from the dessert

parts.note: a mousse is a light creamy pudding

explanation.surface: A dessert from the Orient also goes by the name of an entree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out East' looks like a place, but 'out' removes an E from MOUSSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Moussaka is a Greek baked dish of aubergine and minced meat, served as an entree.

clue.text: Cooked venison I foresee as future possibility

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters have been prepared into a new form

explanation.surface: A cook preparing venison imagines what lies ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' rearranges VENISON and I.
explanation.definitionFit: To envision is to picture in the mind something that might come about.

clue.text: Don protects a 'small-time politician

indicators.note: protects means the Spanish gentleman wraps round the letters like a shield

parts.note: a Don is a Spanish gentleman, a señor
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A Spanish nobleman shields a minor politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small-time' looks like 'minor', but it gives the short form T.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, a legislator.

clue.text: Possibly collect a fish in it

indicators.note: in it tells us the fish goes inside the word just supplied

parts.note: a means per, as in ten pounds a week
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Perhaps go and gather a fish found in something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collect' looks like a verb but is a noun: a short prayer in church liturgy. 'a' means 'per', as in 'so much a head'.
explanation.definitionFit: A collect is a short liturgical prayer, so it is one example of the broader category.

clue.text: Reprimands classes

definitions.meaning: a rating is a scolding
grades or rankings

explanation.surface: Telling-offs for the various grades.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both scoldings and categories of rank.

clue.text: Pale and sickly, though resolute if given time

indicators.note: if given says the answer would become the resolute word only if a T were added, so that word less T

parts.note: doughty means brave and resolute

explanation.surface: A pallid invalid who would be tough given time.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer plus T would be DOUGHTY, so DOUGHTY loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Doughy describes a pasty, unhealthy complexion like raw dough.

clue.text: Commit indiscretion when taking on trainer, say?

definitions.meaning: to say or do something tactless
read literally: putting on a sports shoe, the trainer being one example

explanation.surface: Making a gaffe while pulling on a sports shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: A trainer is British for a sports shoe or sneaker; you put your foot in it when you wear it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make an embarrassing blunder.

clue.text: It may be a player's forte, however

definitions.text: It may be a player's forte, however

parts.words: It may be a player's forte, however
parts.note: forte is the musical direction for loud; the keyboard instrument whose full name pairs soft and loud has a short name meaning the opposite of loud, hence however

explanation.surface: Something a musician excels at, nevertheless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forte' looks like a strength, but it is the musical term for loud; the instrument's everyday name is the term for soft, so it contradicts the forte.
explanation.definitionFit: The instrument's full name is pianoforte, and its short name is the musical direction for soft.

clue.text: A Welshman climbing over one is unaffected

indicators.note: over means the reversed name lies across the numeral, enclosing it
climbing in a down clue means the name reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Evan is a typical Welsh name
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Welsh mountaineer over a hill is unpretentious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns EVAN to NAVE and 'over' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means artless and innocent, without pretence.

clue.text: A portion allotted out of consideration

parts.note: a part is a share given out

explanation.surface: A share assigned out of kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of consideration' looks like 'from kindness', but it means set aside, as in 'joking apart'.
explanation.definitionFit: Apart means excluded or set aside, as in 'that apart'.

clue.text: Spy protecting monarch in a foreign country

indicators.note: protecting means the spy word surrounds the monarch like a bodyguard

parts.note: an agent is a spy
R stands for rex or regina, a monarch

explanation.surface: An undercover agent guards a king while abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' puts R inside AGENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a South American nation, foreign from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: Old archdeacon, given money, is prepared to cook

parts.note: Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon
the ready is slang for cash

explanation.surface: An elderly churchman, handed cash, is getting ready to do some cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: An archdeacon in the Church of England is addressed as 'the Venerable', abbreviated Ven.
explanation.definitionFit: Oven-ready food has been prepared so it needs only to be put in to cook.

clue.text: Well-groomed squadron leader with national emblem

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, taken here from squadron

parts.note: the leek is the national emblem of Wales

explanation.surface: A smart RAF squadron leader sporting a national badge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squadron leader' looks like the RAF rank; 'leader' just takes the first letter of 'squadron'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleek means smooth and glossy, neat in appearance.
